subject.title: perf: bound publisher profile, membership, and catalog reads

question: What completeness contract should `getPublishedDisplayManifest` provide for GitHub-backed publisher profiles: a bounded paginated view, a bounded summary plus on-demand catalog fetch, or an explicitly capped manifest?
rationale: The remaining work is not only mechanical: choosing a read bound requires deciding which display-manifest consumers need complete catalog data and what user-visible fallback is acceptable.

options.title: Adopt bounded summary plus on-demand catalog
options.body: Return profile metadata and bounded counters from the display manifest, then load catalog pages through the existing kind-specific pagination path when a consumer needs entries.

options.title: Keep a complete manifest with an explicit cap
options.body: Document and enforce a finite maximum catalog size, including a clear overflow behavior for large GitHub-backed publishers.

options.title: Split to a focused follow-up
options.body: Close the staged work as partial only after a separate owner-backed issue defines the display-manifest contract and acceptance tests.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded summary plus on-demand catalog
recommendation.body: Return profile metadata and bounded counters from the display manifest, then load catalog pages through the existing kind-specific pagination path when a consumer needs entries.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the merged staged optimization and recorded the unresolved design boundary in the issue discussion.
